questions.question: Into how many distinctive types of territories was the Harshvardhan’s Dynasty divided?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Two**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Harshvardhan's Dynasty was divided into **two distinctive types of territories**.
 
• The two types of territories were the directly administered territories and the feudatory states.
 
• Directly administered territories were under the direct control of the king and his administration.
 
• Feudatory states were semi-autonomous and ruled by local chieftains who owed allegiance to Harshvardhan.
 
• This division helped in the efficient administration and control of the vast empire.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Harshvardhan** was an Indian emperor who ruled North India from **606 to 647 CE**.
 
• He was a member of the Vardhana dynasty and was known for his administrative capabilities and patronage of arts and culture.
 
• Harshvardhan's reign is noted for the consolidation of a large empire in northern India and the promotion of Buddhism.
 
• His capital was at **Kannauj**, which became a prominent center of culture and learning during his rule.
 
• Harshvardhan's administration was characterized by a centralized system with a well-organized bureaucracy.
 
• He is also known for the **Harshacharita**, a biography written by his court poet, Banabhatta.

questions.question:
Read the following about the impact of Green Revolution to the farmers in India.

A. The introduction of the Green Revolution helped the farmers in raising their level of income.

B. Farmers ploughed back their surplus income for improving agricultural productivity.

Identify the INCORRECT statement/statements.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Neither A nor B**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** **Impact of Green Revolution on Farmers in India:**

__
 
• The **Green Revolution** was a period when agriculture in India was converted to an industrial system due to the adoption of modern methods and technology such as **high-yielding variety (HYV) seeds, tractors, irrigation facilities, pesticides, and fertilizers**.
 
• **Statement A:** The introduction of the Green Revolution helped the farmers in raising their level of income. This statement is correct. The Green Revolution led to an **increase in agricultural production**, which in turn increased the income levels of many farmers.
 
• **Statement B:** Farmers plowed back their surplus income to improve agricultural productivity. This statement is also correct. Many farmers **reinvested their increased income** into their farms to further enhance productivity by purchasing better seeds, fertilizers, and farming equipment.
 
• As both statements A and B are correct, the answer is **option 2) Neither A nor B**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Green Revolution in India was a significant period of agricultural transformation that began in the 1960s.
 
• The main goal was to increase food grain production, particularly wheat and rice, to make India self-sufficient in food.
 
• M. S. Swaminathan is known as the “Father of the Green Revolution in India,” he played a crucial role in introducing high-yielding variety (HYV) seeds.
 
• Norman Borlaug is known as the “Father of the Green Revolution.” 
 
• **Technological Advancements:**
 
 
• HYV Seeds
 
• Mechanization
 
• Irrigation
 
• Chemical Inputs (fertilizers and pesticides)
 
 
 
• **Impact:**
 
 
• Significant increase in the production of wheat and rice, especially in states like Punjab, Haryana, and Uttar Pradesh.
 
• Boosted the agricultural economy and reduced dependency on food imports.
 
• This led to changes in the rural economy and lifestyle, including increased income for farmers.
 
 
 
• **Challenges:**
 
 
• Environmental Issues: Overuse of chemical fertilizers and pesticides led to soil degradation and water pollution.
 
• Inequality: Benefits were not evenly distributed, with larger farmers gaining more than smaller ones.

questions.question: Under the Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana (PMJDY), _______ of households provided with a Jan Dhan Account in Madhya Pradesh as on August 09, 2023.

• Under this scheme, every household is encouraged to have **at least one bank account** to ensure financial inclusion and access to financial services like savings, credit, insurance, and pensions.
 
• This achievement reflects the significant progress made in **financial inclusion** and the government's commitment to ensuring that every household has access to basic banking facilities.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

questions.question: Which of the following article of Indian Constitution is related to the Finance Commission of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 280**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 280** of the Indian Constitution is related to the **Finance Commission of India**.
 
• The Finance Commission is constituted by the **President of India** every **five years**.
 
• Its purpose is to define the financial relations between the central government and the individual state governments.
 
• The Finance Commission makes recommendations on the **distribution of tax revenues between the Union and the States** and among the States themselves.
 
• It also addresses issues related to grants-in-aid to the states from the Consolidated Fund of India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The Finance Commission** is a constitutional body for the purpose of allocation of certain revenue resources between the Union and the State Governments.
 
• It was established under **Article 280** of the Indian Constitution.
 
• The **first Finance Commission was constituted in 1951.**
 
• The **Sixteenth Finance Commission** was constituted on **31.12.2023 with Shri Arvind Panagariya,** former Vice-Chairman, NITI Aayog as its **Chairman**.
 
• The recommendations made by the Finance Commission are advisory in nature and not binding on the government.
 
• It plays a critical role in maintaining a stable and efficient fiscal federal structure in India.

questions.question: Green revolution can also be termed as:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Agricultural revolution**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Agricultural revolution** is another term for the **Green Revolution**.
 
• The Green Revolution refers to a set of research, development, and technology transfer initiatives that occurred between the 1940s and the late 1960s, which increased agricultural production worldwide, particularly in developing countries.
 
• Key elements of the Green Revolution include the development of **high-yielding varieties of cereal grains, expansion of irrigation infrastructure, modernization of management techniques, distribution of hybridized seeds, synthetic fertilizers, and pesticides to farmers**.
 
• The Green Revolution led to significant increases in food production and helped many countries to achieve food self-sufficiency.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The term **White Revolution** refers to the **dairy development movement in India**, also known as **Operation Flood**, which made India one of the largest producers of milk and milk products.
 
• The **Blue Revolution** pertains to the management of water resources that led to the growth of the **aquaculture industry**.
 
• The term **World Revolution** is not commonly used in the context of agricultural advancements.

questions.question: Which of the following is the highest award for dance in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sangeet Natak Akademi Award**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**The **Sangeet Natak Akademi Award** is the **highest award for dance in India**.

__
 
• It is given by the **Sangeet Natak Akademi**, India's National Academy for Music, Dance, and Drama.
 
• Established in 1952, the award recognizes individuals for their outstanding contribution to the performing arts, including dance.
 
• The award includes a citation, a plaque, and a cash prize.
 
• Recipients of this award are considered to have made significant contributions to the cultural heritage of India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__

 
• The **Sangeet Natak Akademi** was established by a resolution of the **Ministry of Education, Government of India**, and inaugurated on 28 January 1953.
 
• It functions as the apex body in the field of performing arts in the country, preserving and promoting the vast intangible heritage of India's diverse culture.
 
• The Akademi has played a crucial role in the revival and promotion of traditional and classical dance forms in India.
 
• It also organizes festivals, exhibitions, and seminars to promote the understanding and appreciation of performing arts.
 
• In addition to the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award, the Akademi also confers fellowships and other awards to recognize and honor distinguished artists.

questions.question: Which of the neighbouring countries used to be parts of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Pakistan and Bangladesh**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Pakistan and Bangladesh** were parts of India before the partition in **1947**.
 
• India was divided into two independent dominions, **India and Pakistan**, through the **Indian Independence Act 1947**.
 
• Pakistan was later further divided to create **Bangladesh in 1971** after the** Bangladesh Liberation War.**
 
• The partition was based on religious lines, with Pakistan intended as a homeland for Muslims and India for Hindus.
 
• This historic event led to significant demographic changes and large-scale migrations.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Before the partition, the Indian subcontinent was under British colonial rule.
 
• The decision to partition India was announced by the last Viceroy of India, **Lord Mountbatten**, on **3 June 1947**.
 
• The partition resulted in the creation of two new sovereign states, India and Pakistan, on 1**5 August 1947**.
 
• The partition led to extensive violence and turmoil, with estimates of up to 2 million deaths and millions displaced.
 
• The borders were drawn by the **Radcliffe Line**, named after its architect, **Sir Cyril Radcliffe**.

questions.question: The Service Tax, a tax on services like telephone services, stock brokers, health clubs, beauty parlors, dry cleaning services, etc., was introduced in _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1994-95**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Service Tax** was introduced in India in the year **1994-95**.
 
• It is a tax levied on services provided, including **telephone services, stock brokers, health clubs, beauty parlors, and dry cleaning services**.
 
• The introduction of Service Tax marked a significant shift in the tax structure, aiming to widen the tax base and increase revenue.
 
• The responsibility of collecting the Service Tax lies with the Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs (CBIC).
 
• The Service Tax regime has undergone several changes and reforms since its inception to streamline and simplify the tax process.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Service Tax** was initially introduced at a rate of **5%** and has seen several rate changes over the years.
 
• In **2017**, Service Tax was subsumed under the **Goods and Services Tax (GST)**, which aims to simplify the indirect tax structure in India.
 
• The GST now covers a wide range of services and goods under a unified tax regime, replacing the earlier Service Tax.
 
• The introduction of GST has helped in reducing the cascading effect of taxes and has simplified compliance for businesses.
 
• Service Tax was an essential step towards the modernization and reform of India's tax system, paving the way for the implementation of GST.

questions.question: The "Losar" festival, celebrated in Ladakh and Tibetan communities, marks the _____.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**New Year Festival**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Losar** is celebrated as the **New Year Festival** in** Ladakh and Tibetan communities**.
 
• This festival marks the beginning of the **Tibetan lunar calendar**.
 
• Losar is one of the most significant festivals in the region, characterized by various cultural events, rituals, and traditional performances.
 
• It typically involves offerings, prayers, and festivities that last for several days, symbolizing the welcoming of a new year with hope and joy.
 
• The celebration includes traditional foods, dances, songs, and the creation of intricate sand mandalas.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The term **Losar** is derived from the Tibetan words "**Lo**" meaning **year **and "**Sar**" meaning **new**.
 
• Losar is celebrated not only in Ladakh and Tibet but also in other Himalayan regions like Nepal, Bhutan, and India’s Sikkim and Arunachal Pradesh.
 
• The festival usually falls in the month of **February or March**, depending on the lunar calendar.
 
• Preparations for Losar begin well in advance, with homes being cleaned and decorated, special foods being prepared, and new clothes being worn.
 
• Losar is also a time for family reunions and community gatherings, fostering a sense of unity and cultural identity.
